questions.answer: Primarily for the unique personal experiences/ personal development made possible in exchange. As well as all of the above.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
That St Andrews is a renowned university, where I knew that I could get at least as good teaching as I would have in Copenhagen.
And that with St Andrews I would get to experience a wholly different university life than what we have in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I found the experience very satisfactory.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. St Andrews is used to handling loads of international students. The matriculation process was quite straightforward and well communicated.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
University shuttle bus from airport to St Andrews.
If you stay in a hall (university accommodation), there will be people there to greet you and give you all the information needed.

During matriculation week (the first week of the semester), you will be able to meet with your academic advisor if needs be to talk about your module choices. To confirm your module choices, you will get an appointment with the university where you will talk to a member of staff about your preferences. It is not possible to know for certain, that you will be able to get a spot on your preferred modules before matriculation week. Each module has a cap on the amount of students, that can take it. However I found, that they were able to be flexible, as me being able to get all 30 ECTS credits transferred depended upon getting to specific modules.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A number of different university halls.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Most halls have the option of having 3 meals a day prepared for you.
If you prefer, you can also get a room in an apartment as university accommodation. Here you will live with a number of flatmates and prepare meals on your own in a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You should know, that most students living in university accommodation are first-year students. In Scotland, that means that most people will be around 18 years old. Some halls have predominantly american students. All housing in St Andrews is expensive, including university accommodation. I paid around 32.000 DKK for 3,5 months, including 3 meals 7 days a week. This was the cheapest option available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In many ways it's great to stay in university accommodation. It makes being an exchange student a whole lot easier, and you won't have trouble finding people to talk to. However I did get tired of living with mainly 18-years olds. And I did start missing making my own meals. I kind of felt like I was back at my danish 10. grade efterskole. But overall I would recommend staying in uni accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
They have a web portal, where you send your application to the university. It takes a couple of hours, but it is generally quite easy. You should be aware that you have to get a recommendation from an academic staff at UCPH (could be an instructor), and you have to take the TOEFL english proficiency test, which costs around 2000 DKK.

You will receive emails from the university which will guide you through the process. You will probably feel like you'll be missing information at some points, but that's just cause it's a long process. Just trust that everything will work out if you follow the steps in the emails they send you, and that they will send you information in due time as according to their own schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance on the web page was generally quite extensive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I ended up being successful, but at first it was declined. However, when I spoke to my academic advisor we were able to figure it out.
Be aware, that you won't register for classes (called modules in st andrews) before the first week of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just trust the process and the information they give you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Overall I would say, that the academic programme was satisfactory. The biggest problem for me as a political science student was, that they don't have a political science department, but an International Relations department.
One of my two modules (Politics of the European Union) was very much like what we are used to from UCHP.
The other module (Political Order and Violence in the Middles East) was quite different, and to be honest I probably never quite figured out what the teacher exactly wanted from us. It was not a comparative politics approach, but rather historical sociologist, which was challenging.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was generally similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
As an honours student (3-4th year student) in political science you will have very contact hours. For each of my two modules, I had a 1 hour lecture followed by a one hour seminar. In the seminars you will be just 6-10 students with the lecturer teaching the module, which was quite nice.

This in turn means more time being spent on reading. The semesters are generally quite short (they run from mid september until Christmas, so you will be only be there for 3,5 months) but also quite intense. More emphasis is placed on essays written throughout the semester. Writing the essays were great experiences as they were a whole lot more free than what we are used to from Copenhagen. Subject, approach, theory, method etc can be chosen by yourself, and you will typically get 4-5000 words to elaborate on your thesis.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are loads of different societies and sports clubs that you can join. Nearly anything imaginable.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played tennis and joined the hill-walking society Breakaway. I think there are some 200 different societies and perhaps 80 different sport clubs that you can join. St Andrews is very good in that way.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go see the highlands.
Visit Inverness and Loch Ness.
Maybe rent a car and see Isle of Skye.
Join a Scottish folk dance society (Caledonian dance).
Watch a football match in Glasgow.
Go dipping in the ocean.
Buy a bike and visit the nearby fishing villages (Crail, Anstruther...)
Join some societies and sports clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. St Andrews feels very international more so than Scottish, as there are a lot of english and american students. And students from all over Europe in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay in university accommodation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Scottish hospitality and general friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go there if you would enjoy living in a small town where the entire city feels like a university campus.
2) I think it is generally a quite easy place to be an exchange student
3) But there are a lot of very young students, so be prepared to have patience with them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: All of the above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making international friends and experiencing different ways of being and living in this world.
